subject: gov.policy

milestone: Adopted at the close of the second ordinary session, 2026-08-19
position_end: Recommendations adopted after a plenary session running 5 to 19 August on the public administration facing the digital transition, calling for an affirmed national digitalisation policy of wider scope, a durable national financing mechanism for the sector, adequate power supply, stronger public-agent skills and specialised digital training, and public-private partnerships
note: an advisory council's recommendations; nothing binds government to act and no response is on record

subject: gov.policy
name: National data governance strategy
milestone: Support mission convened with the ministry, 2026-05-13
position_end: Under development with regional-commission and donor support; terms of reference issued by the ministry in April 2026

subject: gov.policy
name: Tchad Connexion 2030
milestone: Launched with US$1.5bn of planned investment to 2030, developed with World Bank support and external analysis
position_start: No record at the window's opening
position_end: In force as the umbrella strategy, targeting at least 80 per cent national internet coverage and about 80 per cent mobile penetration by 2030; its regulatory components - reform of the regulator, privatisation of the state operator, a third operator and number portability - have no dated delivery on record
sources: 2025-07-18-techafricanews-tchad-connexion-2030-strategy-1-5b|2025-12-10 Chad Finalizes Digital Law to Align National Framework With Global Standards|2026-03-16 Chad uses national biometric registry to boost govt systems interoperability
note: No published implementation report, expenditure statement or monitoring framework is held, and the horizon is rendered by 2030 in one account and within six years in another

subject: gov.legislate
name: CEMAC payment systems regulation as Chad's operative payments law
milestone: Regional regulation of 21 December 2016, directly applicable
position_end: Chad has no standalone national digital-payments statute. The operative law is the regional framework, directly applicable as a member state, and the central bank's own register names Reglement n. 03/CEMAC/UMAC/CM of 21 December 2016 on payment systems among the constitutive instruments in force. The national layer is contractual instead: the finance ministry pressed the four payment establishments for a framework convention in February 2026 and signed partnership conventions with them days later
note: a country whose payments law is regional and whose payments practice is contractual has no national statute a citizen can be pointed to

subject: gov.legislate
name: Cybercrime law
milestone: Loi 009/PR/2015; ANSICE reform promulgated 23 March 2026; cybercrime unit created 1 June 2026
position_start: A 2015 statute with no implementing body reformed since
position_end: The regulator's own register of the laws it works under names Loi n. 009/PR/2015 on cybersecurity and the fight against cybercrime, alongside Loi n. 008/PR/2015 on electronic transactions and Loi n. 007/PR/2015 on the protection of personal data. Decret n. 148/PR/2026 of 23 March 2026 promulgated the law ratifying the January 2026 ordinance reforming the national agency for computer security and electronic certification, widening its remit to cybersecurity, personal data, electronic transactions, cybercrime, video surveillance, drones, social platforms and artificial-intelligence systems; the Senate had ratified it 58 votes to 3. Decret n. 2010/PR/2026 of 1 June 2026 then created a cybercrime unit inside the agency and appointed its coordinator and deputy
note: the register names the statutes without linking their texts, and no prosecution, caseload or enforcement figure under any of them is published

subject: gov.legislate

subject: gov.legislate
name: Loi 009/PR/2015 on cybersecurity and Loi 008/PR/2015 on electronic transactions
milestone: Named in force by the regulator's own register of laws
position_end: The sector regulator's register of the laws it works under names Loi n. 009/PR/2015 on cybersecurity and the fight against cybercrime, Loi n. 008/PR/2015 on electronic transactions and Loi n. 007/PR/2015 on the protection of personal data as the operative statutes. The 2026 reform of the computer-security and electronic-certification agency was made against them, the government stating the 2015 frame had become insufficient
note: the register names the statutes and links none of their texts, so the base holds their existence and not their content

subject: gov.legislate
name: Loi 026/PR/2019 organising statistical activity
milestone: Founding statute with four application decrees
position_end: The statute makes the statistics institute the central body of the national statistical system and gives it the status of a public administrative establishment with legal personality; four application decrees sit under it. It is also the instrument the microdata access policy is grounded in. Two instruments have been made under it in the window for the third census: a joint arrete of 6 May 2026 setting provincial, departmental and sub-prefectoral census commissions, and a decret of 20 July 2026 extending the main enumeration to 6 August 2026

subject: gov.legislate
name: Loi n 013/PR/2014 on electronic communications and postal regulation, as amended
milestone: The Senate ratified the amending ordinance on 2025-12-23 by 65 of 67, after the National Assembly on 2025-10-22 by 105 to 31 with 2 abstentions; the ordinance was signed 2025-08-05
position_end: In force with article 18 amended; the amending ordinance's text is not held, so the article's current wording cannot be stated
note: The 2014 law is held only as a degraded scan with a proxied date; the two accounts number the instruments differently, and the amendment's subject is described as licence award conditions while the held article sits under sanctions

subject: gov.legislate
name: Statutory regime for artificial intelligence
milestone: Absence stated by UNESCO, June 2026
position_end: UNESCO's country profile, drawn from Chad's own readiness assessment, finds that Chad regulates cyberspace, that some provisions are obsolete and that at this stage no liability regime for artificial intelligence exists. Chad stated its adherence to the 2021 UNESCO recommendation at the first global dialogue on AI governance in Geneva in July 2026 and called for artificial intelligence that is ethical, frugal, balanced and sovereign; no national strategy is adopted. The March 2026 reform of the computer-security agency does name artificial-intelligence systems within its widened remit, which is the only statutory mention held
note: a dated, cited absence: the assessment names what is missing rather than the base failing to look

milestone: No enacted text, number or gazette reference, the function having been folded into the security agency on 2026-03-13
movement: No change, administering agency now named but no law
position_start: None enacted and no authority; the base holds no Chadian data-protection statute at any date
position_end: None enacted and no authority, with the security agency empowered to administer a regime that does not yet exist

milestone: Adopted by 138 votes to 1 at a plenary of the 2026 first ordinary session
position_end: Adopted, its scope being the collection, processing, retention, use and destruction of biometric data exclusively within judicial and judicial-police procedures
note: The gazetted text is not held, so retention periods, destruction procedure, oversight body and any requirement of judicial authorisation are unknown; deputies raised concerns in debate about inappropriate use

subject: gov.protect
name: Ordonnance n 001/PR/2026 reforming the security and electronic certification agency
milestone: The Senate ratified after National Assembly approval
position_start: A cybersecurity and electronic-certification agency, with no data-protection, artificial-intelligence, drone or video-surveillance remit on record
position_end: A mandate covering cybersecurity, personal-data protection, electronic-transaction security, cybercrime, protection of the national information space, video-surveillance systems, drones, social media, digital services and artificial-intelligence systems, plus a classification of entities of vital digital importance and expanded investigative and enforcement powers
note: Data protection and artificial-intelligence governance sit inside the security agency, and there is no separate data-protection authority. The hub records a vote of 58 to 3 with no abstentions and an ordinance number, neither of which is in any held source

milestone: Validated by the monetary union's ministerial committee 21 December 2023

subject: gov.standards
name: ATNOR and the standardisation law
milestone: Ten international standards adopted as draft national norms, 5 August 2026
position_start: A standardisation agency with no adoption on record
position_end: The standardisation law creates the agency, a national quality council and an interministerial regulation committee, and charges the agency with turning international standards into national ones and with participating in regional and international standardisation. Three dated adoption sessions fall inside the window: the national electrotechnical committee on 31 July 2026, the quality management systems committee on 5 August adopting ten international standards as draft Chadian norms, and the petroleum products committee on 7 August. In March 2026 the agency signed a cooperation protocol in Paris with the French standards body to structure the national system and align it on international standards
note: the ten are adopted as draft norms; no published register of Chadian standards in force is held

subject: gov.standards
name: Regulator service-quality audit programme
milestone: The fifteenth cycle conducted September to October 2025, with findings reported February 2026
position_start: The programme running, its last recorded enforcement being an August 2023 fine of FCFA 5bn on one operator for deteriorating network quality
position_end: The fifteenth cycle found improved urban signal stability alongside faulty equipment, inadequate maintenance, unstable power supply and some sites entirely offline; operators were reprimanded again in December 2025 and June 2026, with no new fine recorded
sources: 2026-02-13 Chad Plans 50 Telecom Sites, 50 km of Fiber in N'Djamena|2026-06-26-connectingafrica-telcos-network-upgrades-airtel-moov|2025-09-02-afriqueitnews-operateurs-connecter-fibre-nationale

subject: gov.standards

milestone: Inaugurated by the minister
position_end: Real-time monitoring of data traffic, network performance, infrastructure failures and spectrum use, with oversight of mobile operators, internet providers, satellite signals and very small aperture terminals
note: Described by the regulator as a shift from compliance-based to continuous data-driven regulation; no cost, supplier, data-retention rule, legal basis or output from the platforms is on record

name: Internet governance forum and non-governmental policy input
milestone: Regulator petitioned by a citizens' organisation, August 2026
position_start: A forum with no binding mandate
position_end: The one standing multi-stakeholder mechanism is the national internet governance forum, self-described as created in 2014 to debate public internet policy between government, regulator, civil society and private sector on the Tunis Agenda principles; it carries no binding consultation mandate. Two dated instances of input sit inside the window: a three-day workshop opened on 18 May 2026 drafting the first national data governance strategy, whose participants included technology incubators and information-security specialists; and a citizens' organisation which formally petitioned the regulator on 28 August 2026 over network coverage and quality, citing over 500 signatures and more than 70 documented testimonies after a thirty-day deadline to the operator expired unanswered
note: the forum page carries no publication date and no record of any consultation it has fed

subject: infra.connect
name: Retail price of internet access
milestone: Head of state ordered a 30 per cent cut, 29 December 2021
position_start: A cut instructed and never audited
position_end: The highest official statement of the affordability position is an instruction, not a tariff schedule: a 30 per cent cut across all internet offers ordered by the head of state on 29 December 2021, reported as reaching 60 to 78 per cent on some segments, against a stated target of moving the cost of internet for a minimum-wage earner from 17.8 per cent of salary in 2020 into a band of 8 to 2 per cent. The ombudsman reported in October 2025 that electronic communications should be treated as a social right, and the minister of state accepted high costs, insufficient quality and weak market regulation. In June 2026 the telecommunications minister argued publicly for the restoration of unlimited satellite internet offers
note: no published tariff schedule, price basket or audit of the 2021 instruction is held, so five years on nothing establishes whether the cut was made

After a fire at the Farcha thermal plant in late July 2026, load-shedding in parts of the capital had run for close to a month by 20 August, with the utility stating that restarting the burnt sets needs new equipment and giving no date

status: Not held, no arrangement on record and the constraint documented
milestone: Solar plant inaugurated September 2025 with 12 MW of 50 MW injectable
position_end: No power arrangement for the national data centre or for telecom sites is on record. The constraint around them is: a 50 MW solar plant at Djermaya was inaugurated on 28 September 2025 over 46 hectares and 81,340 panels, and the head of state stated the same week that the national network can take only 12 MW of it. After the Farcha thermal plant fire of late July 2026, parts of the capital had been load-shed for close to a month by 20 August with no restart date. A separate instruction to migrate transmission sites to renewable power is held as its own row
note: nominal generation added is not available capacity for a critical load, which is the finding

subject: infra.energy
name: Solar mini-grids for five towns
milestone: Ministerial inspection of equipment in manufacture, 6-7 January 2026, with delivery contracted for July 2026 at the latest
position_start: No position held on the second phase; the first phase had already delivered 133,000 individual household solar kits and electrified sixty-one health centres and sixty-two schools in three provinces
position_end: Equipment in manufacture for hybridisation of local grids at five towns, with twelve towns to have solar plants at project end; no delivery confirmation is held
note: World Bank-financed with a Chinese supplier; the July 2026 delivery date has passed with nothing on file either way, and power is the constraint the operators cite for network quality

subject: infra.capacity
name: Information technology equipment transfer to the national police
milestone: Handover ceremony
position_end: Delivered: seventy-four desktop computers, fifty-nine laptops, 105 surveillance cameras, internet-protocol communication equipment, printers, scanners, copiers, videoconferencing and sound equipment, and everything needed to restore the force's public hotline
note: Nothing is stated about training, camera or hotline data retention, or the legal basis for the surveillance capability

subject: infra.capacity
name: Information technology workforce and regulator technical staffing
status: Implemented, output published and establishment not
milestone: Specialist ICT school graduated 121 in its fifth promotion, December 2025
position_end: The national higher school of information and communication technologies, a public higher-education, research and innovation establishment created by ordinance of 2 March 2015 with legal personality and financial autonomy, graduated 121 laureates of its fifth promotion on 17 December 2025 and received 45 computers from the national ICT agency in July 2026. The World Bank's country diagnostic finds digital skills scarce and public platforms built in silos with no shared infrastructure, secure networks, common standards or interoperability across administrations
note: no establishment figure, vacancy rate or technical headcount for the regulator or for government ICT posts is published

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Average loss per online job scam
milestone: Comparative study published August 2026
position_end: An average of 58,000 FCFA per incident for Chadian victims, against 132,000 FCFA for Cameroonian victims; 70% of the Chadian cases described are localised SMS and voice phishing rather than the WhatsApp-based, Nigerian-network-linked social engineering that dominates in Cameroon
note: a research study's survey of respondents, not a reported-crime series; no sample size or national loss total is carried in the record held

subject: infra.cybersec
name: National cybersecurity strategy
milestone: Work launched in December 2022, with no adopted strategy on record
position_start: Work under way since December 2022, with no text
position_end: Work under way, with no text, no adoption record and no publication
note: Known only from a single relayed sentence; no strategy document, launch date or adoption record is held

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Order on the conditions of use of satellite internet services
milestone: Signed by the Minister of Telecommunications
position_end: In force: every user - individual, company or public institution - must be formally identified with the regulator or a licensed operator, giving full identity, residence or registered address, legal references and the serial numbers of modems, routers and antennas; the operator must retain internet addresses and connection history for at least twenty-four months; sanctions run to twelve-month suspension, permanent withdrawal, seizure of non-compliant equipment and administrative fines
note: The order's own number and text are not held, and identification and retention are mandated ahead of any data-protection law

subject: infra.cybersec
name: Tripartite data-centre security audit and certification agreement
milestone: Agreement signed between the digital agency, the security agency and a private firm
position_end: In force, covering audit and certification of the national data centre against critical-infrastructure standards and the operation of one hundred micro-data centres; no completion date, cost or certification result is reported
sources: 2026-02-06 ADETIC, ANSICE, and TECHSO-GROUP Join Forces to Protect Chad's Digital Infrastructure|2026-02-06 Chad Moves to Secure National Data Center Ahead of Launch
note: A United States firm separately offered to audit and certify the same facility in May 2026, and no source connects the two mandates

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Accession to the regional digital integration programme
milestone: Chad's active integration set for the programme's second deployment phase
position_end: Planned, with no accession date, financing share or named component
note: A single mention in a mission read-out

subject: dpi.exchange
name: CEMAC transit interoperability (SIGMAT, SYDONIA World and CAMCIS)
milestone: Cameroon Customs expert mission, fieldwork 21-30 April 2026
position_end: A Cameroon Customs mission supported by AFRITAC Centre assessed interoperability between Cameroon's CAMCIS and the SYDONIA World platform Chad and the Central African Republic use, and prepared implementation of the CEMAC regional SIGMAT transit-tracking system; no implementation date, cost or interface specification is published
note: Binds three named states’ customs systems: Cameroon, Chad and the Central African Republic.

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Central bank accession to the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System
milestone: Accession announced, with member-state banks to connect by end-2026
position_start: The central bank was not a member
position_end: Acceded, with connection of member-state banks and financial institutions targeted for end-2026
note: No Chadian bank is named and the end-2026 target is untested

subject: dpi.exchange
name: National interoperability and data-exchange layer
status: Not held, bilateral protocols in place of a layer
milestone: Tax and treasury protocol April 2026, extended to customs and the central bank July 2026
position_end: Chad has published no national interoperability framework, referentiel or technical standard. The national ICT agency states that it coordinates government information systems to ensure their interoperability, and publishes no standard, schema or exchange rule against that mandate. What exists instead is a chain of bilateral protocols: the tax and treasury directorates agreed automated, secured, real-time exchange of assessments, collections, arrears and payments on 1 April 2026, extended on 21 July 2026 to customs and the central bank. The first phase of a national data governance strategy closed on 21 May 2026 naming interoperability among the priorities to be reinforced
note: point-to-point agreements between administrations are not an exchange layer, and no technical specification for any of them is published

subject: dpi.exchange
name: Prohibition on ministry systems incompatible with existing platforms
milestone: Reported in the 2027 budget orientations
position_end: No ministry may henceforth put in place a computer system incompatible with the existing platforms, and tax, customs, treasury, budget, accounting, cadastre, identity, state property and land registry are to interconnect on a single identifier
note: The budget-framing text is not held and the ministry site was unreachable; the event date is unestablished, and no cost, phasing or implementing agency is named

milestone: Partnership signed
position_end: Signed: the operator is to run awareness campaigns, field deployment and message and call-centre document distribution, and the identity agency is to verify customer data and interconnect systems
note: Wires subscriber data into the identity register with no data-protection authority on file overseeing it

subject: dpi.id

milestone: Memorandum signed with an international migration organisation
position_end: Signed, with no budget, target population size or duration stated

milestone: A real-time data-sharing agreement concluded with the finance ministry
position_start: Operating, with a refugee enrolment pilot running on it and thousands of refugee identification numbers issued by May 2025, and no ministry interconnection on record
position_end: Framed as the intended single source of truth, with real-time sharing live to the finance ministry and private-sector connection offered including for credit checks; no enrolment total has ever been published

subject: dpi.id
name: National identification enrolment total and coverage rate
status: Implemented, no national enrolment total published
milestone: Identity system operating from 29 centres; 3 per cent held ID cards at appraisal
position_start: Three per cent of Chadians holding an identity card (2023)
position_end: The identity agency's own site states that its integrated population and secure-documents system, after enrolment and deduplication, assigns every enrolled individual a unique national identification number, including refugees and residents in transit, across 29 centres nationwide, under the 2016 ordinance that founds it. The World Bank's project appraisal put only three per cent of Chadians holding a national identity card and 0.1 per cent receiving government-to-person payments digitally. Enrolment has since been extended by decision rather than by campaign: agents posted permanently in embassies from September 2025, Sudanese refugees enrolled at Abeche from November 2025, and a memorandum with the migration organisation in May 2026 covering returnees, displaced people and migrants
note: no cumulative enrolment figure and no coverage rate is published by the agency; the three per cent is a 2023 appraisal figure and nothing updates it

subject: dpi.pay
name: Airtel Money Chad
milestone: Licensed as a payment institution in 2023
position_end: Operating and licensed

subject: dpi.pay
name: Consumer protection in payments
milestone: Loi 005/PR/2015 promulgated after adoption on 12 December 2014
position_end: The national consumer protection statute fixes the general frame of consumer protection and applies it to all consumption transactions in goods, services and technologies, listing fundamental rights and creating a national consumer council. It names no payment or financial technology regulator, so the payments-specific supervision the question asks about rests on the regional payments framework rather than on this statute
note: no complaint, redress or sanction under the statute involving a payment service is held

subject: dpi.pay
name: Electronic payment terminals delivered
milestone: Three thousand smart terminals delivered to the finance ministry under the World Bank operation
position_end: Three thousand delivered, with no deployment schedule, target sites or per-agency allocation stated

name: Exclusive electronic state-payment regime
status: Planned, effective from the start of 2027

position_start: Mandated for budget year 2026 - exclusively bank or mobile payments, with cash and cheques out
position_end: The same commitment restated with a 2027 start date; nothing in the base shows the 2026 mandate operating

subject: dpi.pay
name: Framework agreement on mobile payment of public services
milestone: A working session with four operators at which the minister called for rapid signature
position_end: Not signed on the record; the parties named are the two mobile-money operators and two Chadian fintechs
note: Nothing on file since February 2026 shows it concluded

milestone: Partnership announced
position_end: Announced for mobile, terminal and message access across Central Africa with Chad first; no launch date, financing figure or user target

milestone: A multichannel wallet in service, licensed in 2025
position_start: Launched in 2025 as the first wholly Chadian payment institution
position_end: A wallet over mobile application, web portal, unstructured supplementary service data without internet, and a messaging platform, carrying transfers, merchant and bill payments, mass payouts and code acceptance
note: Year precision on the licence; no user, agent-network or transaction figure is published

subject: dpi.pay

milestone: Payment-institution approval obtained in April 2026, on the operator's own filing
position_end: A full payment institution - deposits, withdrawals, account-to-account transfers, cross-border remittances and merchant payments - with FCFA 500m of paid-up capital, solvency norms, cybersecurity audits, anti-money-laundering obligations and client-balance ring-fencing

subject: dpi.pay

milestone: Annual figures for 2025 presented at Douala
position_start: Operating, with Chad a participant state
position_end: Operating, with 20.3m transactions worth FCFA 863bn in 2025 across 153 participants, and a tariff revision workshop under way at the end of July 2026
note: No Chad-disaggregated figure for the switch exists in the base

subject: dpi.pay
name: Regional interoperable QR-code standard
milestone: Launched at Douala under the monetary union regulation of 8 April 2026
position_end: The standard is in force across all six member states including Chad, routed and settled through the regional switch and secured with a personal identification number
note: No Chadian bank, wallet or merchant deployment is on record: Chad is covered by the regulation rather than shown live

subject: dpi.pay
name: Standardised electronic invoice
milestone: Mandatory from the 2026 budget, with exclusive use as the basis for state payment starting 2027
position_end: Launched, Chad being among the first states in the monetary community to do so, with the exclusive-use regime starting 2027
note: No count of invoices issued, taxpayers enrolled or systems connected is published

subject: dpi.registry
name: Birth registration within the legal deadline
milestone: Territorial administration ministry data for 2024
position_start: No dated figure held; the last survey figure is 25.7 per cent of under-fives registered in 2019
position_end: 48.33 per cent of new births registered within the three-month legal deadline, with about 2.95m under-fives undeclared and 829,000 pupils in school with no document attesting their legal existence
note: Three accounts round the undeclared total to 2.948m, 2.95m and 2.958m

subject: dpi.registry
name: Cadastre, state property and land registry platforms
milestone: E-Conservation in production 2 October 2023; 261 state reserves registered 2026
position_start: A paper deeds system under the 1967 land law
position_end: The 1967 land law is still the operative instrument: registration is the procedure by which ownership is established, the titre foncier is the registered title, and custody of deeds and inscription of transfers sit with the conservateur de la propriete fonciere. The digital layer went into production on 2 October 2023 as E-Conservation, the computerised domains and land conservation system, with the first 5,000 secured deeds distributed. Since then a geospatial firm was engaged in December 2025 to update the national mapping, modernise the cadastre and build a land information system; a Chad-France protocol of April 2026 covers digitising cadastral archives held in France; a joint arrete of 17 August 2026 puts cadastral data in front of the judges hearing land disputes; and an interministerial committee reported 261 state reserves recovered, enumerated and registered in August 2026
note: the 261 reserves are the only registration count on record; no national total of titles, parcels or digitised deeds is published

subject: dpi.registry
name: Child birth-registration campaign
milestone: Launched with a first phase of six months to December 2026
position_end: Running, targeting at least a million children aged four months to seventeen years across twelve provinces by household enumeration plus a schools campaign, with community teams using smartphones feeding the biometric register; no enrolment achieved to date is reported
note: One account puts the household component in twelve provinces and another says it will cover every province

subject: dpi.registry
name: Digital civil registration
milestone: Launched on African Identity Day
position_start: Did not exist as a launched national programme
position_end: Launched, with municipal interoperability work under way from April 2026; no coverage or throughput figure is published
note: The architecture is reported as message transfer from registry offices, hospitals, camps and mobile units to the identity agency for validation

subject: dpi.registry
name: Fichier electoral
milestone: 8,204,830 electors registered for the December 2024 polls
position_end: The most recent published national figure is 8,204,830 registered electors for the coupled legislative, provincial and communal elections of 28 and 29 December 2024, 8,173,058 of them inside Chad and 31,772 abroad. Partial legislative and senatorial elections of 20 and 21 June 2026, convoked by decret of 22 May 2026, put the electoral agency under an explicit obligation to revise the register within the deadline; nothing held confirms the revision was carried out. In June 2026 the permanent political dialogue framework published a roadmap whose second strategic objective runs from a reliable electoral register to equitable party financing
note: the 2024 figure is a press relay of official data rather than the primary act, and no revised total for 2026 is published

subject: dpi.registry
name: MJS CONNECT youth and sports association register
milestone: Launched in N'Djamena 2026-09-04
position_end: Launched by the youth and sports ministry to register sports federations, youth associations and movements and build a national directory of them, letting registered associations enrol, hold a digital space and file administrative formalities online, and recording who is active, in what field, where and with what results, with performance indicators intended to inform how the ministry allocates resources
note: no registration count, cost, vendor or data-protection provision is published; training in its use is announced for the coming months, and the minister set it against youth activity concentrated in the capital

subject: dpi.registry
name: Moratorium on court fees for supplementary birth judgments
milestone: Signed 2026-02-02, suspending fees for children aged four months to seventeen years until 2030
position_end: In force to 2030, the four-year legal suspension inside which the six-month registration campaign runs
note: The instrument's own text is not held; its signing date and terms are known only from launch statements

subject: dpi.registry
name: National business register and one-stop shop
milestone: Register computerised February 2020; one-stop-shop digitalisation in review
position_end: The regional business-law organisation handed Chad the integrated local-registers and national-file software and equipment for four local sites on 28 February 2020, World Bank-financed. The one-stop shop for company creation is not yet digital: a technical workshop of 18 February 2026 validated its digitalisation, explicitly a review rather than a deployment. In August 2026 the commerce ministry restated what the register does not do — registration alone never authorises a regulated activity, and naming an activity in the statutes or the extract does not replace a licence
note: no count of registered businesses, of sites connected to the national file, or of companies created online is published

subject: dpi.registry
name: Registre Social Unifie
milestone: 684,500 households registered under the 2025-2030 strategy
position_end: The unified social registry is described as a centralised, dynamic, spatially aware database interoperable with other systems, carrying 684,500 households under the adaptive social protection strategy for 2025-2030. Its pastoral component enumerated 37,449 households across 13 provinces and more than 250 pastoral concentration zones by March 2026, and an adaptive safety-nets project financed at 120 million dollars launched at Mao on 3 April 2026 deploying across nine provinces. Enrolment continues in the capital, and the agencies behind it met in March 2026 on identifying every registry entrant by their national identification number, an accord not yet signed
note: the registry is interoperable in description and not yet in fact: the link to the biometric register was still an unsigned accord in March 2026

subject: dpi.registry
name: Street addressing
status: Not held, one city programme and no national register
milestone: N'Djamena addressing officialised 2016, still incomplete in 2026
position_start: One city programme, no national register
position_end: The only documented Chadian street-addressing programme ran in N'Djamena from 2013 to 2016 at 700,000 euros co-financed by the European Union, the municipal association and the city, defining addressing as city mapping, street codification, enumeration surveys and a simple information system feeding the local tax base. A 2026 survey finds the system still incomplete: numbering begun in 1990 across the first five arrondissements and officialised in 2016, untouched in the old quarters and in some newly planned ones, so official and popular addressing coexist. No national address register exists
note: the 2026 finding rests on a survey of sixty respondents, which is the only coverage statement held

subject: dpi.registry
name: TASDJIL civil-registration application
milestone: Deployment dated to 2021 by the head of the UNICEF national sub-office
position_end: Deployed since 2021 as part of civil-registration modernisation, with no coverage, site count or throughput figure published; new monthly paper collection forms were introduced with UNICEF support in August 2026 to improve transmission of birth, marriage and death data to the centre
note: Year precision, from a single sentence of a UNICEF official's remarks; no source connects it to the digital civil registration programme launched in September 2025

subject: dpi.registry
name: Taxpayer register and the eTAX platform
milestone: Data-exchange protocols signed with treasury April 2026 and customs and the central bank July 2026
position_end: The tax directorate's platform covers tele-registration, tele-declaration and tele-payment, alongside a mobile application and a normalised electronic invoicing system. A protocol of 1 April 2026 with the treasury provides automated, secured, real-time exchange of tax issuances, receipts, arrears and payments, extended on 21 July 2026 to customs and the central bank
note: no taxpayer count is published on the platform, so the register’s size is not established

subject: dpi.mis
name: CREDOP and the national police information system
milestone: Inaugurated 10 September 2025; created by decret of 18 August 2023
position_end: Decret n. 2278 of 18 August 2023 created the centre for collecting and recording police data at the public security ministry, charged with managing the national police information system and with collecting, centralising, safeguarding and sharing data. The centre and a forensic-science sub-directorate were inaugurated on 10 September 2025, European-financed under the national arm of the regional police information programme launched in 2016
note: nothing states how many police stations feed the system, or whether any outside the capital do

subject: dpi.mis
name: Education management information system (StatEduc)
milestone: Ministry statistics and digitalisation staff trained 20-25 July 2026
position_end: In use in the higher-education, research and vocational training ministry, whose statistics and digitalisation staff were trained on questionnaire and database configuration, deployment and updating of data-entry masks, extraction, consistency checking and database validation; no coverage figure or published output is held, and nothing is on file for the basic-education ministry
note: Sits under the Programme de Refondation de l'Ecole Tchadienne, financed by the Global Partnership for Education and implemented with UNESCO support, and is reported by UNESCO

subject: dpi.mis
name: Education management information system decentralisation
milestone: Effective in 16 provinces across 12,863 primary schools (2025)
position_start: Paper collection at school level, keyed centrally
position_end: As at 2021 school-level collection was on paper, carried up the hierarchy and keyed manually into the central system, with no digital capture at the schools. Decentralisation of the system is now effective in 16 provinces across 12,863 primary schools, to be extended to seven more, through eight academies, 24 provincial delegations, 129 inspectorates and 380 pedagogical sectors, with data still analysed centrally. About 550,000 dollars of computing equipment — 8 servers, 168 all-in-ones, 115 laptops, 21 tablets and storage — was handed to seven provincial delegations and four central directorates on 15 June 2026
note: the ministry's own education compact records the system as weakly decentralised and donor-dependent, with teacher headcounts differing between it and the budget

subject: dpi.mis
name: Electronic medical records and health-facility interconnection
milestone: Exploratory meetings on a Washington mission of late May 2026
position_end: Exploratory only - electronic medical records and interconnection of health facilities discussed, with no contract, pilot or system named
sources: 2026-07-01 Chad and US Explore Partnerships on Satellite Connectivity and Cybersecurity|2026-06-01-digitalbusiness-washington-partenariats-tech

subject: dpi.mis
name: Judicial information system
milestone: Digital exchange platform presented 23 October 2025
position_end: Under the national strategy for digital transformation of the judicial system, the justice ministry with United Nations development support launched a digital exchange platform between litigants, lawyers and the judicial system, presented on 23 October 2025 — the first document establishing that a judicial information system exists in Chad at all. In February 2026 the Supreme Court received laptops, desktops, professional scanners, server-room equipment and network hardware through a European-funded parliamentary and electoral support project
note: no case count, court coverage or go-live statement for the platform is held

subject: dpi.mis
name: National health management information system
milestone: National launch of DHIS2 November 2022; data watch centre inaugurated June 2026
position_start: Legacy system, no national platform held
position_end: The health ministry moved from its legacy system to DHIS2 through a 2021 pilot in Moyen-Chari and Batha and a national launch in November 2022, with 96.4 per cent of districts entering data directly into it after the first year. In June 2026 it inaugurated a data watch centre under the national digital-health plan for 2025-2030, a national platform to consolidate, analyse and visualise health data, and in April 2026 committed to a patient-centred electronic medical record with Rwandan technical assistance, integration with DHIS2 among its stated benefits
note: no completeness, timeliness or data-quality figure for the system is published beyond the first-year district-entry rate

subject: dpi.mis
name: REDISSE Phase IV regional disease-surveillance operation
milestone: Implementation completion report issued 30 November 2025
position_end: A US$280m five-country regional disease-surveillance operation, closed by the World Bank's implementation completion report of 30 November 2025, carrying a health information and ICT subcomponent at 14% of the sector share and naming DHIS2, IDSR and EWARS among its systems; the held capture is an excerpt and states no country-specific system, coverage or outcome
note: Angola, the Central African Republic, Chad, the DRC and Congo, with ECCAS.

subject: dpi.govtech
name: e-BNFT land freight bureau platform
milestone: User training opened in a foreign port city, 1 September 2026
position_end: The national land freight bureau opened user training on its digital platform in Douala on 1 September 2026, for transporters, freight forwarders and drivers, covering user-account creation, file entry and operation tracking, with practical modules run by two technology suppliers. The chair of the bureau's digitisation steering committee said the sessions answer a request users made at the platform's official presentation, and that since February 2026 the bureau has worked to extend digitisation across all its agencies and posts, naming seven locations including two in Cameroon
note: a landlocked country's freight bureau training users in a foreign port city is the fact worth holding; no user count, transaction volume, platform launch date or agency-by-agency coverage is published

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Electronic visa as the sole visa channel
milestone: Provided for from 2027 in the budget orientations
position_end: Planned as the exclusive channel for application, payment, processing and issue from 2027
note: The base holds no statement on whether an electronic visa operates today, and exclusivity is stated with no fallback channel

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Freight bureau enrolment platform
milestone: Presented at an official ceremony at Douala in Cameroon
position_end: Live for enrolment, launched to Chadian hauliers working in Cameroon; no services list, deadline, fee schedule, platform address or enrolment target is stated
note: Nothing on file relates it to the transport ministry's own planned platform

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Fully online business creation
milestone: Provided for from 2027 in the budget orientations
position_end: Planned for end-to-end online filing, fees, identifiers and delivery of official documents
note: A continental development bank programme separately funds interconnection of business one-stop shops

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Guidam sovereign data platform
milestone: Biennial delivery report on the presidential programme produced through the platform, received 2026-08-07
position_end: In use as the government's sovereign digital data platform for tracking delivery of the president's twelve-project programme; the Prime Minister received the two-year delivery report drawn from it on 7 August 2026, ahead of a cabinet seminar to align implementation reporting
note: no custodian, supplier, hosting arrangement or public access to the platform or its data is stated, and the report itself is not held

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Integrated public financial management system
milestone: The whole expenditure chain mandated through the system from the 2026 budget
position_end: Operating as the mandated expenditure environment, with the 2027 orientations extending it to all institutions, local authorities, public establishments, projects and diplomatic and consular missions
note: No coverage figure, no count of entities live and no implementing agency is named

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Integrated transport-services platform
milestone: Discussed at a ministerial meeting, with nothing further on file
position_start: Planned, with nothing on record being built
position_end: Planned, with nothing on record being built - eleven months with no dated advance
sources: 2025-09-12 Chad to deploy integrated digital platform for transport services
note: The stated scope is vehicle registration, driving licences, technical inspection, transport licences and permits

subject: digital.localgov
name: Civil-registry interoperability with the capital municipality
milestone: A working session on interoperability between the biometric system and communal registers
position_start: A francophone civil-registration programme running in two provinces, with no municipal interoperability on record
position_end: A commitment to support the capital's digital transition and extend the model to other institutions, with no completion date or scope
sources: 2026-04-28-tribuneechos-anats-oif-etat-civil-interoperabilite|2025-08-12 La Francophonie supports birth registration efforts across Central Africa, Madagascar
note: The only local-government item the base holds for Chad

subject: digital.localgov
name: Local-government digital services beyond the capital
milestone: Provincial councils equipped January 2026; 23 communes equipped May 2026
position_end: Local government has hardware and no services yet. On 7 January 2026 each of the 23 provincial councils received two computers, two solar kits, two printers, a photocopier and a satellite internet kit, explicitly to extend the public finance management system to the territorial authorities and to secure and trace local budget circuits. On 19 May 2026 the national digital transformation programme handed the 23 provincial chef-lieu communes 272,964,000 FCFA excluding tax of computing and digital equipment for local electronic services
note: no local digital service, portal or transaction count is named in either handover; what is established is the equipment and not what runs on it

subject: digital.rural
name: Rural connectivity programme for the unserved localities
status: Not held, studies and equipment in place of a programme
milestone: Feasibility studies financed December 2020; solar kits sold from 2025
position_end: No rural connectivity programme for the unserved localities is on record. The European Investment Bank financed three feasibility studies in December 2020 on high-speed broadband, improved telecommunications and connectivity for remote rural communities, described by the Bank as its first targeted digital cooperation with Chad; nothing held reports what they found. What has been delivered is power rather than connectivity: 145,000 subsidised solar kits sold across all 23 provinces at the equivalent of twenty dollars against a hundred, under a programme financed at close to 295 million dollars and targeting a rise in electricity access from 6 per cent in 2018 to 30 per cent in 2027
note: the studies are five years old and their outputs are not held

subject: digital.rural
name: Solar-powered telemedicine kiosks
milestone: Reported in service in rural areas, August 2026
position_end: Solar-powered telemedicine kiosks are helping rural patients overcome distance to care; no kiosk count, operator, consultation volume or funding source is on file

subject: digital.rural
name: Study of another state's agricultural digital solutions
milestone: Delegation studied three platforms in Lome, 28 August 2026
position_end: A four-member delegation from the regional food system resilience programme visited Lome on 28 August 2026 to study three digital agriculture platforms built by the Togolese arm of the same programme - a hydro-agrometeorological information system, an alerting service and an agricultural advisory service - which produced and distributed more than 80,000 agrometeorological and climate bulletins in 2024, reaching more than 122,000 people including nearly 50,000 women
note: a study visit inside a programme both countries belong to; nothing is recorded about what, if anything, is to be replicated here, and the base holds no equivalent domestic platform to compare

subject: tech.ai
name: Deployed or piloted artificial-intelligence system
milestone: Tuberculosis screening reported February 2026; vaccination pilot launched 2 April 2026
position_start: No deployed or piloted system held
position_end: Two sectoral pilots are on record and both are in health. A mobile computer-aided tuberculosis screening strategy screened 7,116 people and took 6,357 X-rays, flagging 589 abnormalities of which 112 were confirmed and all started on treatment, with algorithms tailored to nomadic, internally displaced and refugee groups. Vacci360, launched on 2 April 2026 in Lac, Kanem and Hadjer Lamis, adds an analytical layer over the existing health information system: geographic accessibility, automated micro-plan optimisation, mobility indicators including herd movements and a conversational assistant for querying the data. Elsewhere the state is training rather than deploying — public-works school staff in generative AI in April 2026 and the food-security office in August
note: both pilots are donor- or partner-run; no state-operated production system is held

subject: tech.ai
name: Directorate-general for artificial intelligence
milestone: Created by presidential decret of 21 October 2025
position_end: A presidential decret of 21 October 2025 created a directorate-general for artificial intelligence inside the telecommunications, digital economy and administrative digitalisation ministry and named its director-general — the first standing state structure for artificial intelligence in the Chadian administration. On the research side, an arrete of 3 August 2026 created an interdisciplinary artificial-intelligence research laboratory inside the national development research centre with a mandate to draw up a national AI research plan, following the first national AI scientific days held there from 29 December 2025
note: no budget, establishment or work programme for either body is published

subject: tech.ai
name: National digital transformation and artificial-intelligence strategy (SNTD 2026-2031)
milestone: Consultancy recruitment opened to draft the strategy, August 2026
position_end: A consultancy is being recruited to draft a National Digital Transformation and Artificial Intelligence Strategy for 2026 to 2031; no draft, adoption route or delivery date is on file
note: The procurement notice is the first thing the base holds on an artificial-intelligence strategy for this country.

subject: tech.industry
name: Official sector statistics
milestone: Market observatory for 2024 presented 1 October 2025
position_start: 14.2 per cent internet use and 8.7 million subscribers in 2020
position_end: The regulator's market observatory for 2024, presented on 1 October 2025, gives 5.6 million internet users against 4.8 million in 2023, 14.8 million mobile subscribers up 9.2 per cent, and sector turnover above 237 billion FCFA. It is the first published movement in the series since the 2020 observatory, which had given 14.2 per cent of the population using internet services, 10.0 per cent using SMS, mobile penetration of 53.5 per cent and 8.7 million subscribers
note: a trade report of the same month carries a 2024 industry figure of 38.6 per cent mobile penetration and internet access below 15 per cent, which does not reconcile with the regulator's own observatory

name: Privatisation of the state telecommunications operator
milestone: Re-announced in February 2025 with a 60 per cent stake offered, and no advisory bank appointed
position_start: Announced repeatedly since 2014, with the stake offer re-announced in February 2025 and no advisory bank appointed
position_end: Still no advisory bank appointed; the national strategy re-provides for privatisation without changing the position
sources: 2026-02-16 Waking the dead - Slow road to extinction for Africa's former telco incumbents 11|2025-07-18-techafricanews-tchad-connexion-2030-strategy-1-5b
note: A named-analyst account; staff were cut from about 10,000 to under 500 after a sale and subsequent nationalisation

subject: tech.industry
name: Third private mobile operator
milestone: Named as a component of the national strategy, with no licensing process on record
position_end: Planned only, with nothing on record being licensed

subject: tech.innovate
name: Start-up statute, innovation fund or state innovation instrument
status: Implemented, a fund without a statute
milestone: Youth entrepreneurship fund launched 11 July 2020 at 30 billion FCFA
position_end: Chad has no start-up statute. It has a fund: Loi n. 005/PR/MFB/2020 of 26 May 2020 created the Fonds pour l'entrepreneuriat des jeunes, launched on 11 July 2020 at 30 billion FCFA, lending entirely through banks under a 70 per cent state guarantee at a target rate of about 6.25 per cent, with information and communication technology among the eligible sectors. A state technology hub followed: the Centre d'innovation technologique de N'Djamena, created by arrete of 1 September 2025 and launched on 30 October 2025, covering incubation of Chadian technology start-ups, research laboratories, digital-skills training and a digital library. In December 2025 a Best Challenge Project opened to identify and finance projects across all 23 provinces
note: no disbursement total, loan count or share going to technology ventures is published for the fund, and no tenant or cohort count for the hub

subject: tech.innovate
name: Telemedan
milestone: Company-reported cumulative usage
position_start: More than 2,000 users and about 10,000 consultations reported
position_end: Unchanged; no source in the window refreshes it
note: User and consultation figures are company-reported by the founder; a plan of 100 kiosks reaching a million people over three years has no progress record

subject: capacity.literacy
name: National digital literacy programme
status: Not held, local sessions in place of a national programme
milestone: Regulator sessions from January 2026; a civil-society project running to 2029
position_end: No national digital literacy programme exists. What runs is local and small: the national ICT development agency opened free intensive digital-skills sessions at Bongor in January 2026 — computer initiation, office software and internet safety — for an expected hundred beneficiaries, paired with a disinformation-awareness campaign. A civil-society project with the education ministry, running from October 2025 to September 2029 across N'Djamena's seventh and ninth arrondissements, Moundou, Dobara, Sarh and Mandoul, records that fewer than 30 per cent of 15-to-30-year-olds in its target areas hold digital skills, and reports around a 75 per cent skills gain across more than 150 young people trained in its pilot
note: the under-30 figure is the project's own for its target areas, not a national measurement

subject: capacity.training
name: Refugee digital learning centre
milestone: Inaugurated at a one-stop shop in the east, funded by Italy
position_start: One pilot centre for young refugees and the host community, with extension to other eastern towns stated as an intention
position_end: Unchanged - no extension recorded
note: No cohort numbers at either end

subject: capacity.training
name: Specialist ICT higher education
milestone: 121 laureates graduated in the fifth promotion, December 2025
position_end: The national higher school of information and communication technologies, created by ordinance of 2 March 2015, graduated 121 laureates of its fifth promotion on 17 December 2025 and received 30 desktop and 15 laptop computers from the national ICT agency on 14 July 2026 for its laboratories, teaching and research. The education framework statute of 2006, 129 articles and in force, charges technical and vocational secondary education with developing learners' capacity to adapt to technological change and creates no digital curriculum or computing stream
note: no breakdown of the 121 by programme, and no employment outcome for any cohort, is published

subject: capacity.training
name: Youth digital and financial inclusion training
milestone: A two-day session for 120 young people in the capital
position_start: Nothing held at the window's opening
position_end: One hundred and twenty young people trained in digital tools and financial inclusion, with girls and women prioritised
note: A single cohort rather than a standing programme, delivered under the continental bank's microfinance grant

subject: capacity.training
name: Youth digital innovation and employment training programme
milestone: Launched at a maker space with the national employment office and a francophone body
position_start: Nothing held at the window's opening
position_end: A first cohort of seventy-five in training against a target of 150, on tracks in digital craft and design and in embedded electronics and connected objects, with the funder supplying equipment and consumables
note: No budget figure is stated

subject: include.access
name: Citizen feedback channels
milestone: Ombudsman complaints website launched 27 February 2026
position_end: The only standing channel the base held was the Presidency's online suggestions form, addressed to the civil cabinet, resting on no enacting law or decree. On 27 February 2026 the ombudsman launched a website taking citizen complaints online with case tracking, in French, English and Arabic. The general policy declaration of the Fifth Republic government commits to putting the citizen at the centre of law and policy making through digital innovation, via an inclusive law-making mechanism and a citizen oversight mechanism
note: no case volume, response time or enabling instrument is stated for either channel

subject: include.access
name: Cost of connectivity
milestone: Ombudsman report of 29 October 2025 accepted by the minister of state
position_start: A cut instructed and never audited
position_end: The ombudsman presented a report on 29 October 2025 arguing that electronic communications should be treated as a social right; the minister of state accepted high costs, insufficient service quality and weak market regulation and undertook to implement the recommendations. The standing instrument behind the position is the head of state's December 2021 instruction of a 30 per cent cut across all internet offers, against a target of moving the cost for a minimum-wage earner from 17.8 per cent of salary into a band of 8 to 2 per cent
note: a stated government position on affordability, not a tariff instrument, and no price series for Chad is held

subject: include.access
name: Digital inclusion of persons with disabilities
milestone: 400 disabled traders enrolled with an identity-linked document, July 2026
position_start: A project target and nothing delivered
position_end: The only quantified national commitment is a project one: the digital transformation project financed at 92.2 million dollars targets about 40,000 direct digital-training beneficiaries including at least 25,000 women and girls and 2,000 people with disabilities. Two deliveries are on record. From 27 July 2026 the social action ministry and the identity agency began enrolling 400 people with disabilities — 115 visual, 285 physical — trading on the N'Djamena-Kousseri road, issuing free of charge a secure document tied to the national identification number with a QR code for authentication by customs and police. In May 2026 a three-month vocational programme for people with disabilities in the capital carried an informatics module among three
note: no accessibility standard applies to any Chadian digital service, and no national count of people with disabilities reached is published

subject: include.access
name: Francophone civil registration project, Chadian component
milestone: Reported on the continental civil registration day
position_start: Nothing held at the window's opening
position_end: More than 53,000 children registered in two provinces, with a second phase in preparation
sources: 2025-08-12 La Francophonie supports birth registration efforts across Central Africa, Madagascar
note: The organisation's own claim, with no independent verification and no value stated

subject: include.access
name: Gender equity in digital access
milestone: Project target of at least 25,000 women and girls trained
position_end: The only quantified national commitment on gender in digital is a project target: the digital transformation project financed at 92.2 million dollars targets about 40,000 direct digital-training beneficiaries including at least 25,000 women and girls, alongside broadband access for over four and a half million rural people
note: no sex-disaggregated figure for internet use, mobile ownership or ICT employment in Chad is held, and nothing reports progress against the target

subject: include.access
name: Health-facility-integrated civil registration
milestone: Reported to an international identity assembly
position_start: More than 120,000 children registered through hospital-based registry offices since 2023, ninety-seven digitised hospital registration points, and more than 180,000 pupils registered in school campaigns
position_end: Unchanged - no update in the window
sources: 2025-06-03 Chad, Mali, Senegal pursue birth registration reforms to close gaps
note: A practitioner account; the stated plans are to raise digitised hospital points from ninety-seven to six hundred and to reach zero unregistered births by 2030

subject: include.access
name: Refugee biometric identification
milestone: More than 4,000 refugee identity numbers issued in the capital
position_start: More than 4,000 issued against a pilot target of 7,000 for the capital and 25,000 across expanded phases
position_end: Unchanged - no issuance figure after 2025-05-01, though the identity agency received further enrolment equipment reported in March 2026
sources: 2025-05-09-biometricupdate-refugees-biometric-ids-idemia-unhcr|2026-03-16 Chad uses national biometric registry to boost govt systems interoperability
note: A World Bank-funded pilot with the refugee agency and the national refugee commission, on a French supplier's technology

subject: include.divides
name: Rural and urban split of internet access
milestone: Fifteenth quality-of-service audit in the field, October 2025
position_end: The regulator's fifteenth national mobile quality-of-service audit measured coverage province by province rather than nationally: 94 points in Hadjer-Lamis, Lac and Kanem with coverage on twelve strategic road axes, continuing into Barh el Gazal and Borkou, and 20 points in Chari-Baguirmi and Mayo Kebbi Est. It was opened on 16 September 2025 after the fourteenth audit found both operators missing their licence indicators. Skills follow the same geography: a project running to 2029 records fewer than 30 per cent of 15-to-30-year-olds holding digital skills in its target areas outside the capital
note: the audit measures coverage at points, not households connected, so no rural-urban split of internet access as such is published

subject: data.statistics
name: National statistics development strategy 2021-2025
milestone: Adopted by decret of 14 October 2021
position_end: The strategy was adopted by decret in October 2021, and 126 of 234 sustainable development indicators had a published baseline at the 2024 assessment. The World Bank is financing the national statistical system at 105 million dollars, more than a third of it for the third population and housing census and for human resources, and 78 bursaries to regional statistics schools have been granted. The institute trained 90 national and regional journalists on the statistical system and the census over three days in November 2025
note: the strategy's period ends in 2025 and no successor is held

subject: data.statistics
name: National statistics institute data publication
milestone: Five data portals listed by the institute; access policy under the 2019 statistics law
position_end: The statistics institute publishes through five named channels — an Open Data Portal, a national data summary page, a national statistical data archive, an SDG goal tracker and an indicator tracker for the national development plan — under Loi n. 026/PR/2019, which makes it the central body of the national statistical system with legal personality and financial autonomy. Access is conditional: microdata may not be copied or transmitted without prior written agreement, a prescribed source line must be used, and two copies of any report must be supplied to the institute
note: no dataset count, update cadence or download figure for any of the five channels is published

subject: data.statistics
name: Third general population and housing census
milestone: A decree of 2026-07-20 extended the main enumeration to 2026-08-06
position_end: Main enumeration closed 2026-08-06 after an extension expressly for sweeps, coverage having been acknowledged incomplete at the original deadline; no results, preliminary or otherwise, are held
note: Neither census decree is held, Chad having no reachable online gazette and the statistics institute's site no address record; days from the close, one nomadic district had still not seen an enumerator

subject: data.open
name: Access-to-information statute
status: Not held, no such statute has been adopted
milestone: Absence stated by UNESCO at the 45th Universal Periodic Review
position_start: No statute, and applications for online newspapers open
position_end: UNESCO's periodic review filing states at paragraph 13 that no freedom of information law has been adopted in Chad, and at paragraph 19 recommends one be introduced to international standards, against a constitutional guarantee at article 28 of the 2018 constitution. The direction since is the other way: on 3 August 2026 the media regulator suspended, until further notice, the examination of applications to create online newspapers, and stated that offences on digital platforms fall outside its remit for now
note: a dated, cited absence rather than an unexamined one

subject: data.open
name: Open government data portal or policy
status: Implemented, portals without a policy and without open terms
milestone: INSEED's five data portals; microdata access policy grounded in the 2019 statistics law
position_end: Chad has adopted no national open-data policy or charter. What exists is diffusion infrastructure: the statistics institute lists an Open Data Portal, a national data summary page, a national statistical data archive, an SDG goal tracker and an indicator tracker for the national development plan. The terms are not open — the archive bars users from copying or transmitting microdata to anyone without prior written agreement, requires a prescribed source line and two copies of any report produced, grounded in the 2019 statistics law. A digital Journal Officiel launched on 14 May 2026 gives free access to legal texts and procurement notices back to 1958, and a water geoportal was presented in June 2026
note: portals exist and reuse is restricted, which is the opposite of the usual gap: the pipes are built and the licence is not

subject: data.satellite
name: Earth observation for agriculture
milestone: Crop-monitoring brief of January 2026
position_end: The standing operational use of earth-observation data for Chadian agriculture is a donor-run one: a country brief prepared using satellite crop monitoring alongside a cereal balance sheet, food-price monitoring and the regional food-security framework, whose 2026 outputs put the 2025 cereal harvest 9 per cent above average. The national space agency has published a two-pillar roadmap naming an observation microsatellite whose stated priorities are agriculture, climate, water management and disaster prevention, and a longer-term national constellation; neither carries a date, budget or decret
note: the operating capability is foreign and the national capability is a roadmap

subject: data.satellite
name: Space cooperation protocol with a national space agency
milestone: Protocol of agreement signed at N'Djamena
position_end: A memorandum only, covering spectrum and satellite-communications management and remote sensing for resource mapping, with no financing, hardware, date or deliverable; a follow-up delegation visited the digital agency in February 2026
note: The only earth-observation item the base holds for Chad

subject: geopol.usa
name: Cybersecurity cooperation with the United States infrastructure security agency
milestone: A videoconference following Chadian attendance at a counter-ransomware summit in Washington
position_start: Collaboration axes agreed on threat monitoring, engineer training and incident response, with nothing signed
position_end: Unchanged; no source in the window reports any follow-up

subject: geopol.usa
name: United States digital work programme
milestone: A mission held in May 2026 and a readiness to support conveyed on 2026-06-29, with nothing signed
position_start: No work programme on file, United States contact being limited to a ministerial meeting with the charge d'affaires on 2025-11-26
position_end: Four priority areas agreed - digital infrastructure, satellite connectivity, cybersecurity and digital health - with no instrument signed; a supplier stated its willingness to audit and certify the national data centre, a mandate already held by the tripartite agreement of February 2026

note: The two accounts give different mission dates, and the minister flagged United States visa refusals for Chadian technical personnel as a delivery risk

subject: geopol.china
name: Chinese grant agreements of August 2026
milestone: Two agreements signed 2026-08-20
position_end: Two grant agreements totalling 300 million yuan, in tranches of 100 million and 200 million described by the minister of state as immediately mobilisable, which the Chinese side says will finance infrastructure and social development while supporting digital technologies
note: the FCFA equivalents in circulation differ between outlets — 25bn, 26.4bn — on their own conversion dates; no project list or digital allocation is published

subject: geopol.china
name: Chinese technology and AI scholarships
milestone: Announced at a ministerial audience 2026-08-17
position_end: A programme of 5,000 scholarships in technology and artificial intelligence announced by the Chinese ambassador to the telecommunications and digitalisation minister
note: no monetary value, selection route, timetable or host institution is stated

subject: geopol.china
name: Fifth-generation platform request for the state operator's mobile arm
milestone: A ministerial request made to the supplier in China, with no decision, funding or delivery on record
position_start: Requested in 2024, with nothing on record
position_end: Unchanged as at February 2026

subject: geopol.china
name: Huawei as contractor for the state connectivity programme
milestone: Named as contractor for the national data centre and the backbone, with a supervising engineer
position_end: Unchanged; a December 2025 ministerial meeting with a regional delegation produced no agreement, figures or timeline
sources: 2025-01-10-agenceecofin-tchad-centre-donnees-national-finalisation|2025-12-29 Chad Steps Up Rollout of Tchad Connexion 2030 in Talks With Huawei

subject: geopol.eu
name: European digital-governance or regulatory-alignment instrument
milestone: Digital Journal Officiel launched 14 May 2026 on European funding
position_end: The European Investment Bank's December 2020 cooperation — three feasibility studies on high-speed broadband, improved telecommunications and connectivity for remote rural communities — is described by the Bank as its first targeted work with the government on digitalisation and rural connectivity. What has since been delivered is state machinery rather than regulatory alignment: the digital Journal Officiel launched on 14 May 2026 was European-funded and built with United Nations technical support; the police data centre and forensic-science unit inaugurated in September 2025 were European-financed under the regional police information programme; and the Supreme Court received computing and archiving equipment in February 2026 through a European-funded parliamentary and electoral support project
note: no European regulatory-alignment instrument — no adequacy process, no data-protection convergence, no digital-trade chapter — is held for Chad

subject: geopol.gulf
name: Gulf-state digital cooperation
milestone: Cybersecurity memorandum signed October 2023; investment agreement promulgated January 2026
position_end: The one Gulf instrument whose defined subject is digital is a memorandum on cybersecurity, cybercrime and international cyber cooperation signed on the margins of Regional Cybersecurity Week in Abu Dhabi in October 2023 by Chad's telecommunications minister. The money came later and is not sector-specific: at the close of the Emirates-Chad trade and investment forum in Abu Dhabi on 10 and 11 November 2025 Chad announced 20.5 billion dollars secured against its national plan, 4.1 billion of it from forty private companies and 16.4 billion in donor pledges, and in January 2026 the President promulgated the law ratifying an Emirates-Chad investment protection agreement
note: the pledged sums are multisectoral; no digital project, disbursement or system delivered under any of them is held

subject: geopol.india
name: Indian digital partnership
milestone: A ministerial meeting at which a memorandum was intended and no timeline was announced
position_end: Still no memorandum or instrument on file
sources: 2025-02-17-tchad-inde-partenariat-numerique|2025-12-02 Chad Accelerates Digital Cooperation to Support Its Transformation Agenda
note: The scope asked for was training of Chadian engineers in artificial intelligence, support to the national information technology school, and digitalisation of postal services including a postal bank

subject: geopol.india
name: The national higher school of information and communication technologies
milestone: Created by ordinance of 2 March 2015; fifth promotion graduated December 2025
position_end: The school is a public establishment for higher education, research and innovation in electronic communications, created by Ordonnance n. 005/PR/2015 of 2 March 2015 with legal personality and financial autonomy, seated in N'Djamena under the posts and new information technologies ministry. It graduated 121 laureates of its fifth promotion on 17 December 2025 and received 30 desktop and 15 laptop computers from the national ICT agency on 14 July 2026
note: nothing held connects the school to Indian financing or cooperation, which is what this row was opened to establish
